title: Performance: Upgrade `filepath.Walk` to `filepath.WalkDir` to avoid expensive stat calls
body:
There are a couple of lingering usages of `filepath.Walk` in the codebase. 

`filepath.Walk` is known to be inefficient because it makes an expensive `os.Stat` system call on every single file and directory it encounters. Since Go 1.16, `filepath.WalkDir` has been available, which uses `os.ReadDir` under the hood to bypass these expensive system calls entirely.

Currently, `filepath.Walk` is still being used in:
1. `pkg/api/handlers/libpod/quadlets.go`
2. `pkg/api/handlers/compat/images_build.go`

These instances should be modernized to use `filepath.WalkDir` instead. This is a well-known Go performance best practice, and it is especially beneficial during operations that scan directories (like image builds or quadlet processing) on file systems with many files.

I would be happy to submit a quick Pull Request to clean these two instances up if maintainers agree!
